frequency_question: How often do states under existential conventional attack successfully operationalize domestic production of complex foreign guided missiles within two years of acquisition?
membership_rule: Includes states fighting conventional interstate wars that initiated domestic assembly or production lines for high-tech foreign guided munitions; excludes simple maintenance depots and peacetime licensing.

cases.name: Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile series (license/domestic development from US/Israel tech)
South Korea Hyunmoo missile program (tech transfer/domestic production)
Ukraine Neptune missile (indigenous development leveraging Soviet supply chains)
Iran Noor/Qader (reverse engineering and localized production of Chinese C-802)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 10 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (2.5x)
coverage_note: 4 named cases; believed roughly 10 total historical precedents matching high-intensity wartime guided missile localization.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral weapons transfers and early Cold War domestic missile adaptation programs in smaller states lack public granularity.
skeleton: Total documented instances of high-tech missile localization attempts during active conflict or severe embargo vs successful operational lines
multiplier: 4 hits out of 10 major historical wartime/embargoed guided-missile localization attempts
validity_reason: Base rate reflects long-term technological and industrial constraints in wartime, which evolve slowly over decades.
